transcript.text: Bosch KGN34NL3AG - some days it's fine, other days it just clicks every few minutes at the back and doesn't seem to run, and the freezer starts getting soft. Then it starts working again by itself. What's going on?

That is not normal compressor cycling: a single click with a steady running hum can be normal, but repeated clicking every few minutes while the freezer softens means the cooling system is failing to start. The most likely cause is the compressor start/overload device repeatedly trying and failing to start it; next is the compressor itself beginning to seize or overheat. A socket or control fault is less likely, but still possible because it recovers by itself. When it next does it, listen from the lower rear: does each click follow a brief hum or buzz, or is it click-only? In the meantime, keep the doors shut as much as possible and move vulnerable food to another freezer if it is softening; repeated failed starts can eventually become a permanent no-cool fault.
Yes, each click is followed by a very brief hum, and then it goes silent for a few minutes before clicking again. There is no burning smell and nothing has tripped.

The leading possibility is the compressor start relay/overload device; the other possibility is that the compressor itself is becoming hard to start. Poor ventilation or a dust-clogged condenser can make either problem worse, especially when it later recovers by itself. Switch it off and unplug it, then gently vacuum any accessible dust from the rear/lower grille and make sure it is not tight against the wall; do not remove electrical covers or disturb anything attached to the compressor. Is that area dusty or short of clearance? If it is clean with good space and the hum-click cycle continues, it needs a refrigeration engineer to test the start device and compressor rather than guess at parts.

I pulled it out and the back is a bit dusty, but there is a gap between it and the wall. I'll give it a gentle vacuum. If it carries on after that, is it likely to be the start device or the compressor itself? I'd pay up to about £150 for a repair.

If it carries on after the dust is cleared, the start relay/overload device is the more likely and usually more economical fault. The compressor itself is the second possibility, but that is only established when an engineer tests it with a known-good start device and checks the compressor windings—this symptom alone cannot separate them reliably. Your £150 ceiling may be realistic if it is the start device and access/labour are straightforward; a compressor replacement is normally unlikely to be worthwhile at that budget. If the hum-click cycle returns after cleaning, arrange a refrigeration engineer and describe it as “compressor hums briefly, clicks off every few minutes, then the freezer warms”; ask them to test the start/overload device before condemning the compressor. Keep food elsewhere if it starts softening again.
